sentences.text: Later on, victim was recovered on 10/06/2023.
It is further submitted that on recovery, her statements under Sections 161 & 164 of Cr.P.C. have been recorded.
Videography panchnama was prepared.
Charge-sheet was filed.
Appellant abjured his guilt, therefore, trial was conducted and appellant has been convicted & sentenced, as mentioned above.
5. It is pointed out that victim (PW-1) has admitted in Para-5 of her cross- examination that she and the appellant were in love with each other.
They performed love marriage with each other.
She also admitted that she had gone with the appellant on her own volition.
While they were staying at Bhopal, they have informed neighbours that they are husband and wife.
In Para-6 she admits that she had left her home on account of an altercation with her brother and had gone with the appellant.
When she was staying at Bhopal with the appellant she had not given any intimation in regard to her relationship.
She admitted that she was residing along with the sister-in-law and children of the appellant in his house.
Her sister-in-law used to keep her well and she had not given any intimation to her family members.
She further admits that appellant had neither asked her to elope with him nor ever asked NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43153 3 CRA-7377-2024 her to undergo abortion.
She stated that she had performed marriage with the appellant.

6. Mother of the victim (PW-2) has admitted that her marriage was performed 38 years prior to the date of her deposition and she had given birth to her eldest child in the next year of her marriage and thereafter all the girls were born at an interval of one to one and a half years.

7. Father of the victim (PW-4) stated that his marriage was performed 25-26 years prior to the incident and further deposed that he is not literate and, therefore, he cannot say as to whether age of the victim is 18 - 19 years or not.
He further stated that whether age of the victim was recorded on the basis of estimation.
Thus, when testimony of PW-2 and PW-4 is read together, then it is evident that at the time of incident, age of the victim was more than 18 years.

8. Victim has admitted her consent in the relationship and has also admitted that they have performed marriage, therefore DNA report (Ex.P/42) being positive, showing that appellant is the biological father and victim is the biological mother of the product of conception, is inconsequential when the victim herself admits that she had gone with the appellant on her own volition and the prosecution has failed to prove that she was minor at the time of incident.
9. As far as, Ravishankar Nagar (PW-3) is concerned, he stated that he was working as a Head Master in the school where prosecutrix was given admission in lower KG in the year 2013.
She stated that her date of birth is mentioned as 02/10/2007 and she was given Transfer Certificate on 04/07/2018.
However, he could not prove as to who had recorded the date of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43153 4 CRA-7377-2024 birth.

He did not even produce the school admission form and only produced a certificate issued by himself, as contained in Ex.P/18 and Dakhil Kharij Panji ( Ex.P/17-C), but could not give any documentary evidence in support of the date of birth recorded in school records.

Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove the age of the victim to be a minor and it's a case of consent where minor admits the consent and as per the testimony of her parents, she was major at the time of the incident
, therefore, conviction of the appellant under Sections 376(3) of IPC, 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and 5j(ii) /6 of POCSO Act cannot be sustained in the eye of law.
11. Accordingly, appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment dated 09/03/2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Narmadapuram is set aside.
Appellant be released forthwith, if his custody is not required in any other case.
12. Case property be disposed off in terms of the orders of the learned trial Court.
